headline: Roundup worked so well the weeds evolved

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Kill weeds without the plow
slides.text: Farmers fought weeds by plowing, which costs topsoil, time and fuel. **They wanted one weed killer that left the soil alone.**
slides.alt: A snowy hillside field below a tall grassy bank along a fence line, where years of plowing have carried the soil downhill
slides.credit: Plow erosion along a fence line, Whitman County, Washington, 1940s or 1950s. USDA. Public domain.

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: One spray, over 125 kinds of weeds
slides.text: In 1970 Monsanto chemist John Franz found glyphosate, sold as Roundup from 1974. **It controls over 125 kinds of weeds.**
slides.alt: Rows of young soybean plants growing up through the stalks of last year's corn in an unplowed field
slides.credit: Soybeans in a no-till field. Lynn Betts, USDA NRCS. Public domain.

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: The survivors took over
slides.statLabel: weed species in 31 countries resist glyphosate, a 2026 review finds
slides.text: Global use rose almost 15-fold after 1996, when crops engineered to survive it arrived. **Each spraying left behind the weeds it could not kill.**
slides.alt: Broadleaf weeds growing in the gap between two rows of soybeans
slides.credit: Weeds in a soybean field, 2013. United Soybean Board. CC BY 2.0.

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Partly: the record looked clean
slides.text: In 1997 Monsanto scientists found no verified resistant weeds after decades of use. **But weeds had already beaten older herbicides.**

slides.label: Where it stands
slides.title: Still in court, still on shelves
slides.text: A WHO agency called glyphosate probably carcinogenic; US and EU regulators found it unlikely. **Bayer agreed to pay up to $10.9 billion over cancer claims**, admitting no liability.

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: Control of over 125 kinds of weeds
Less plowing, saving topsoil, time and fuel
A key tool behind no-till farming
costs: 62 weed species resistant to it, in 31 countries (2026 review)
Resistant weeds that often survive other herbicides too
Up to $10.9 billion in cancer settlements, no liability admitted (Bayer, 2020)
slides.text: It made weeding cheaper and plowing less necessary. **Leaning on it everywhere wore down what made it work.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: The cure breeds resistance
slides.text: One weed killer on every field killed most weeds and spared the rare ones it could not. **Year after year, those survivors took over.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: Rotate tools before the problem learns them
slides.text: The more one tool is used, the faster the problem adapts to it. **Rotate tools before the problem learns them.**
